name: Hawai'i Sign Language

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page hawa1235 (refs: Rarrick & Lambrecht 2016; Campbell et al. 2022; Woodward 2012)
sources.note: Only one descriptive reference (Rarrick 2015); classification 'Sign Language', independent origin, ~20% cognate with ASL.

sources.citation: Earth, Barbara & Linda Lambrecht. 2021. History of Hawai'i Sign Language and Hawai'i Deaf People (final report), Kaipuleohone LL1-054. hdl:10125/80433

sources.citation: Rarrick, Samantha & Brittany Wilson. 2016. Documenting Hawai'i's Sign Languages. Language Documentation & Conservation 10: 337-346. hdl:10125/24697
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)

sources.citation: Rarrick, Samantha, Jan Fried & Brittany Wilson. 2015. The Sign Language Documentation Training Center. 4th ICLDC (slides + audio). hdl:10125/25276
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)

sources.citation: Rarrick, Samantha. 2015. A Sketch of Handshape Morphology in Hawai'i Sign Language. University of Hawai'i at Manoa Working Papers in Linguistics 46(6), 1-22. hdl:10125/73260
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-; also held in print at Harvard (Tozzer Library (offsite storage), call number L.SOC.53.7.25.12.23)
sources.harvard_location: Tozzer Library (offsite storage), call number L.SOC.53.7.25.12.23
sources.note: Section 2 'Sign language linguistics basics' covers manual parameters (handedness, handshape, location, orientation) and handshape phonology/morphology only; nothing on stress, accent, prosody or movement rhythm (a full-text search for stress/accent|accent|prosod|intonat|rhythm|emphas returns nothing).
